Conditions

Agreed condition rules, consolidated after the wound-table review (issue #1125). Use these timing and sensory rules throughout the current catalog.

Ratings, decay, and persistence

At the end of the affected character's turn, resolve a temporary numbered condition's effect, then reduce its rating by 1. At 0 it ends. A condition gained during that turn also decreases at that turn's end. Numbered instances add where meaningful; binary states do not. Normal Boon/Bane cancellation and caps apply.

The number can describe severity as well as duration (Dazed, Burning), or duration only (Blinded, Paralyzed). A higher duration-only rating does not strengthen the condition. Dazed 3 or greater grants no action categories.

An asterisk means no automatic decay: Blinded 1* is blindness that persists until its specified remedy. It does not mean every such injury is incurable. A wound states whether treatment, replacement, or another remedy removes it. Maintained Grappled does not decay. Binary conditions and lasting wound penalties use their own removal rules.

Spend a Main Action to reduce an appropriate condition on yourself or an adjacent creature by 1 without a roll: staunch Bleeding, extinguish Burning, or warm someone suffering Freezing with a plausible method. This is not a universal cure for every condition. Specialist abilities can remove more or use a cheaper action. A star prevents automatic decay, not a removal method explicitly allowed by its source. Mixed temporary and starred contributions still need a specific tracking ruling; do not assume the star makes later temporary contributions permanent.

Example: untreated Bleeding 3 deals 3 damage, decreases to 2, then deals 2 and 1 on subsequent turns before ending. A Main Action reducing it before the first tick changes that sequence to 2, then 1. Burning and Freezing apply matching resistance to each tick, with the normal minimum 1 damage for a damaging event.

ConditionEffectRemoval / persistence
Burning XFire X damage at end of turn; matching resistance appliesResolve damage, then decay; appropriate Main reduces 1
Freezing XCold X damage at end of turn; matching resistance appliesResolve damage, then decay; appropriate Main reduces 1
Bleeding XX damage at end of turn, bypasses resistanceResolve damage, then decay; appropriate Main reduces 1
Poisoned XX Banes to action/defense/death rolls, not inventory dice; no damageDecay unless explicitly maintained or persistent
Frightened XX Banes while its source is perceptible; no forced choices or movementDecay unless explicitly maintained or persistent; source must be identified
Blinded XCannot see; no direct sight-required targetingDuration only; decay; Blinded 1* requires its specified remedy
Deafened XCannot hear; cannot respond to hearing-only triggersDuration only; decay; Deafened 1* requires its specified remedy
Slowed XSpeed −X, minimum 0Decay unless explicitly persistent
Dazed XAt 1/2/3+, choose 2/1/0 of Main, Maneuver, Reaction; movement remainsChoose at turn start; no retroactive change to spent actions; decay 1 at turn end
Grappled XMovement 0; at 1/2/3+, choose 2/1/0 of Main, Maneuver, ReactionMaintained; no decay. Force reduces 1/2/3 when a Main remains; rating 3 requires help
ProneCrawl; standing costs 2 movementStand or source effect; occupied prone square traversable at cost 2
Asleep XUnaware, no actions/movementDefault numbered decay; adjacent Main wake effort reduces 1; damage ends it; source can specify persistence
Paralyzed XAware, no actions or movement at any positive ratingDuration only; decay; no gradual return of options before 0
UnconsciousUnaware, prone, no actions/movementSource; ordinary healing wakes only HP-caused unconsciousness
PetrifiedInert solid, unaware, no actions/movementSource defines protection and cure
HiddenUniversal hidden state, not observer-specificEnds on attack/open revelation; DA judges concealed movement
InvisibleCannot be seen; not automatically unlocatedSource; attacking ends Hidden, not automatically Invisible

Asleep, Paralyzed, Unconscious, and Petrified apply three defense Banes; overlapping helpless states apply that penalty once. Dazed adds no defense Banes. Attacks against a Grappled creature gain one Boon per level of its Grappled rating, including attacks against grapplers, using normal Boon/Bane rules. When Dazed and Grappled coexist, use the greater action restriction, not their sum.

Grappling restricts the grappler by their own contribution as well as the target. Multiple grapplers' contributions add on the target. Each can freely release even at rating 3, ending their contribution. Once helpless capture is established and combat is over, resolve the scene through ordinary narration.

Example: Paralyzed 3 prevents actions and movement, falls to 2 at turn end, then to 1, then clears. Dazed 3 instead gradually returns action options as it decays. Blinded 2 is full blindness for two decay steps, not stronger blindness than 1.

Provisional prone combat rider for tests: none beyond movement until approved. Do not import automatic melee Boons or ranged Banes from another game's prone rule.

See @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.0ed84bf5cc8bb982.JournalEntryPage.401d23f4b66980ee]{wounds} for lasting effects and @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.1cea11a23d58e328.JournalEntryPage.83082c8f9728466c]{foundations} for movement.

Action-category timing — latest agreement

Dazed and Grappled determine retained action categories at the start of the affected creature’s turn. Changes during the turn do not undo spent actions or recalculate that turn’s category selection. Temporary Dazed decays at turn end; maintained Grappled does not decay. Grappled’s movement restriction still applies while the hold exists. Paralyzed, Asleep and Unconscious retain their immediate restrictions; they are not action-category selection effects.

Mixed-source tracking: record temporary and starred contributions separately. Add effective severity where the condition uses severity; decay only the temporary part. For duration-only conditions, either positive contribution keeps the condition active, without multiplying its effect. Generic temporary reduction removes temporary rating only; permanent treatment follows its source.
